source_document.body:
2026 SEMA Show • This Batmobile-Looking Lamborghini Temerario Is on Display at SEMA
The Chrysler Sebring Coupe Returns to Life With Pacifica DNA, Though Only Across Imagination Land
11 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
Everyone has been pretty busy over the past week across the automotive industry in North America, including Stellantis . They balanced the recently concluded 2026 SEMA Show and other things, but not revivals – at least not of the passenger car variety.
Stellantis did feature a reborn nameplate – the SRT Performance division worked for the first time on a Jeep concept, the Wrangler Scrambler Concept , reimagining the legendary Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler with modern flair. But other than that, they were preoccupied by The Brotherhood of Muscle returning to NASCAR Cup Racing, as Dodge is returning to NASCAR Cup Series racing alongside Ram Trucks and Kaulig Racing, which now serves as the two brands’ anchor team.
What about Chrysler ? Well, the ailing brand hasn’t made the news rounds in an official capacity since August, when Chrysler debuted two custom Pacifica concepts at Roadkill Nights Powered by Dodge in Pontiac, Michigan, on August 8, and only the rumor mill has taken care of it since then. According to the latest reports, the brand will soon become a multi-vehicle marque again with the introduction of the Airflow and the Arrow and Arrow Cross beneath it – giving budget-conscious buyers additional CUV options on the market.
But what about passenger cars? Well, it seems that Pacifica is destined to rule alone from the minivan category, as the three new entries will swell the ranks of crossover SUVs. Not across Imagination Land, though, if this member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has anything to say.
Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a Chrysler car – the return of the Chrysler Sebring mid-size nameplate in coupe format.
The original Chrysler Sebring was produced from 1995 to 2010 in convertible and sedan or coupe body styles, with the two coupe generations created with help from Mitsubishi and produced at the Japanese automaker’s Normal, Illinois facility. Now the unofficial, hypothetical design project imagines the resurrection of the Chrysler Sebring as an affordable mid-size coupe with classic proportions and Chrysler Pacifica’s new visual identity embedded at the front.
Reception from the fans has been mostly positive, and people are saying that “it’s a nice-looking car” and that the Mitsubishi Eclipse Coupe should be coming back, too. Someone also asked for the convertible version to bring back the LeBaron moniker, by the way. That’s all fine and dandy, but what should power this good-looking coupe?
Chrysler could easily borrow the STLA Medium architecture from within the Stellantis ranks and perhaps the standard output version of the 3.0-liter Hurricane inline-six. It could be detuned to around 300 hp with a lot of low-rpm torque grunt in order to keep it affordable and out of Dodge Charger’s way. So, what do you think?
